intro.texto: You look at the sky with your family. A light crosses very fast: it's the Space Station. Someday you want to explore space.
Dr. Itzel Ramos was studying the ice at the Moon's south pole with Chispa, her robot dog. Chispa detected a huge solar storm coming.
The base radio broke, Chispa got lost in a crater, and Itzel is running out of oxygen. Her data could protect Earth's satellites.
All the astronauts are on another mission. Mission Control is looking for someone brave. There's no age limit!

carta.pregunta_motivo: I want to join the rescue because...

motivos.texto: I want to help Itzel and Chispa
motivos.respuesta: A good rescuer thinks of others first!
That sense of responsibility is just what we need!

carta.elegido: You've been chosen. Before you go, you'll complete the mission simulation.

centro_control.inicial: Before we go, there's something very important! We need to carry an extra oxygen tank to help Itzel and Chispa. We can't start the rescue without it!
centro_control.oxigeno_ok: Excellent! We have our oxygen reserve. Now we have 6 kg left for the rest of the gear.
centro_control.oxigeno_fijo: The oxygen tank is REQUIRED GEAR: it stays in the backpack. If you need room, leave an optional object.
centro_control.falta_traje_nave: Stop, astronaut! The door won't open: you don't have a suit and rocket yet. Choose them in the hangar first.
centro_control.falta_oxigeno: Wait, astronaut! We're missing the oxygen tank. Itzel and Chispa might need that reserve to get back safely. Let's go get it!
centro_control.exceso: That's too much weight! We have to choose well. Remember, the oxygen tank is required. To carry {nombre}, free up {kg} kg of optional objects.

reacciones.linterna: Good choice! We'll be able to light up the dark craters and look for Chispa's tracks.
reacciones.radio: Excellent! We could fix the communication with the base.
reacciones.botiquin: A good explorer is always ready for emergencies.
reacciones.comida: Supplies can be useful if our mission takes longer.
reacciones.escudo: This gear can help us boost radiation protection in a shelter.

alerta: Beep, beep! Wait a moment! I'm detecting something strange...
(You hear static... and a faint bark)
It's Chispa! His collar still works. We have to find him!
The base's main radio is broken, but my short-range emergency receiver picked up the signal. Let's go to the Control Center: STELLA will help us analyze it!

mini.mal: Nice try! That signal doesn't match. Look at the pattern again.
mini.bien: You did it! You found Chispa's signal!

stella.bienvenida: Hello, astronaut! I'm STELLA, your mission assistant. Let's review the lunar conditions before starting the rescue of Itzel and Chispa.

tomar.linterna: Good choice! Sunlight never reaches the permanently shadowed craters: the flashlight will help us look for Chispa's tracks.
tomar.radio: The main communication is damaged: with this kit we could restore it.
tomar.escudo: Extra protection against radiation. Remember: in a strong solar storm, the safest place is a shelter.
tomar.botiquin: If Itzel is hurt, we'll be able to give her first aid.
tomar.comida: Supplies in case the rescue takes longer. Every kilogram counts.

dejar.linterna: Without a flashlight, exploring the dark craters will be harder.

dejar.escudo: Without a shield, we'll depend on finding a shelter if there's a solar alert.
dejar.botiquin: Without a first-aid kit, we'll have to be very careful.
dejar.comida: Without food, the rescue will have to be quick.

mision.titulo: MISSION: RESCUE AT THE LUNAR SOUTH POLE
lineas: • Goal: rescue Dr. Itzel Ramos and Chispa.
• Story risk: possible solar radiation event.
mision.aviso: ◆ Mission situation and risks: game simulation.
mision.dialogo: Our priority is to find Itzel and Chispa. We'll have to manage our gear well because we can only carry 10 kilograms.

explica.cadete: There are craters where the Sun never shines. It's very dark there! Chispa's signal comes from there.
explica.explorador: At the lunar south pole there are craters where sunlight never reaches directly. Chispa's signal comes from a very dark area.
explica.especialista: Near the south pole the Sun always looks very low, so the bottom of some craters stays in permanent shadow. Chispa's signal comes from one of those regions.

A.recomendacion: A flashlight could help us look for his tracks.

mas.texto: The Moon's axis is almost straight up: at the poles the Sun barely rises above the horizon. That's why the bottom of some craters hasn't had direct light for billions of years. NASA's LRO probe studies them; there could be ice there.

explica.cadete: It's super cold in the shadow. Our suit protects us!
explica.explorador: Some permanently shadowed areas have extremely low temperatures. Our suit must keep us protected.
explica.especialista: Without sunlight, the ground in permanently shadowed areas gets almost no heat: they're among the coldest places measured in the solar system. The suit must insulate us and save its power.

B.recomendacion: Check that the suit's thermal system and power work before going out.

mas.texto: The Diviner instrument on the LRO probe measured temperatures colder than 200 °C below zero in south pole craters. In the game, basic thermal protection already comes with your spacesuit.

explica.cadete: Sometimes the Sun throws storms. If there's an alert, we go to a shelter!
explica.explorador: Solar storms can increase radiation in space. If we get an important alert, we'll have to find a protected shelter.
explica.especialista: Coronal mass ejections and solar particles increase radiation outside Earth. The Moon has no global magnetic field or thick atmosphere: in a strong event the safest place is a shielded shelter.

C.recomendacion: The protection module can be useful, but during a strong emergency we must reach a proper shelter.
C.fuente: ● Real data: solar storms · ◆ SIMULATION: game alerts

mas.texto: NASA's DONKI database records coronal mass ejections. Record used in the game: {fecha}, at {vel} km/s. The game's alerts are simulated: they are not real NASA forecasts.

explica.cadete: The ground has rocks, slopes, and dust. Let's walk carefully!
explica.explorador: The lunar terrain can be uneven, and dust can damage some equipment. We'll have to explore carefully.
explica.especialista: Lunar regolith is a fine, sharp dust that sticks to everything and can wear down seals and mechanisms. Crater slopes and rocks mean we have to plan the route with the map.

D.recomendacion: Look at the map and choose a safe route.
D.fuente: ● Real data · NASA Moon / Moon Trek

mas.texto: Lunar dust (regolith) is very fine and sharp-edged because the Moon has no wind or water to wear it down. On the Apollo missions it stuck to the suits. NASA Moon Trek shows real maps of the south pole's terrain.
mas.fuente: ● Real data · NASA Moon / Moon Trek — trek.nasa.gov/moon

senal.detecta: I detected a weak signal! It could come from Chispa's collar, but we need to check its pattern.
senal.activa: Chispa's signal is still active! It comes from a region of dark craters. You can check the map if you want.
senal.aviso: ◆ GAME SIMULATION: Chispa's signal and location are part of the story.
senal.explica: We're looking for two short pulses and one long one. Look at the length of each pulse or tap ♪ to hear it.
senal.mal: Nice try! Look at the signals again. We're looking for two short pulses and one long one.
senal.bien: Excellent, astronaut! We've identified the signal from Chispa's collar. Now we know we must get ready to explore a region of dark craters.
senal.mapa: This is Chispa's approximate area (simulation). We still don't know where Itzel is: the search starts here!

rec.linterna: The dark craters can make the search hard. A flashlight could be very useful.
rec.radio: The main communication is damaged. This gear could help us fix it.
rec.escudo: Extra protection can be useful, but remember that a proper shelter is essential against strong solar radiation.
rec.botiquin: If we find Itzel hurt, having first-aid supplies can help us.
rec.comida: Supplies could be useful if the mission takes longer.

eval.falta: We can't start the rescue without the required oxygen tank.

eval.escudo: We have extra protection, but we'll need other ways to get light and communication.
eval.base: We have the oxygen reserve. Every kilogram counts: which tool do you think will help us?

equipo.bit_listos: All set! Board your ship up the ramp.
equipo.bit_falta: You still need to choose your suit and your ship.
equipo.pista: Itzel is far away and a storm is coming: think about what you need more, protection or air.

equipo.bascula_luna: On the Moon everything weighs one sixth as much, but your suit still takes the same effort to move.
equipo.bascula_base: Try on a suit and step on again.
equipo.arco_base: Without a suit all the radiation gets through. Choose one and come back!
equipo.arco_blindado: Look: almost no radiation dots get through the armored suit.
equipo.arco_ligero: With the light suit, lots of radiation dots get through.

tecnicos: At the Moon's south pole there are craters that haven't seen the Sun for billions of years.
Those craters hold water ice: it could give astronauts water and oxygen.
The Moon has almost no air: ships can only brake with their thrusters.
A solar storm shoots out particles at hundreds of kilometers per second.
A day on the Moon lasts almost a month on Earth.

acelerar.cuesta: You burn fuel: landing will be harder.

resultado.guardar: You saved the air for the rescue.

aterrizaje.explicacion: The Moon has almost no air: parachutes and wings don't work. Only thrusters can slow the ship against lunar gravity (1.62 m/s²).
aterrizaje.exito: You touched down at {vel} m/s. Perfect! The Moon has no air: only thrusters slow you down.
aterrizaje.fallo: Hard landing: you hit at {vel} m/s and the safe speed was {segura} m/s. Start braking earlier and in pulses.
aterrizaje.base_texto: Welcome to the base! The airlock closed and you're safe. Before looking for Itzel, get your gear ready.
aterrizaje.bitacora: You landed at the lunar south pole at {vel} m/s.

ruta.expuestos: The storm arrived in {hT} h and the rescue took {hR} h. We were under the storm for {exp} h.
ruta.sin_linterna: Without a flashlight, the dark crater slowed us down.

ruta.sin_linterna_corto: Without a flashlight you go slower.

cresta.cuesta: It's long: more hours outside, more oxygen, and more radiation if the storm arrives.

rescate.llegada: You reach Itzel's last known position… but you don't see anyone.
rescate.chispa_aparece: It's Chispa! He recognizes you and guides you through the rocks.
rescate.itzel_refugio: Itzel took shelter under a rock overhang, just like a real astronaut would.
rescate.radio_titulo: The radio is damaged. You have to fix it to talk to Earth.
rescate.radio_kit: + You brought the radio kit: you fix it fast.
rescate.radio_sin_kit: − You didn't bring the radio kit: it takes longer to fix.

mensajes.explica: The battery only has enough for 2 messages. Which ones do you send?

tormenta.efecto: Earth protects its satellites in time.
tormenta.respuesta: Earth: Got it! We're putting the satellites in safe mode.

ayuda.efecto: A support ship launches: the trip back uses less oxygen.
ayuda.respuesta: Earth: Great news! A support ship is on its way.

hielo.respuesta: Earth: Amazing! That ice will help future bases.

mensajes.viaja: The signal travels at the speed of light: it takes {s} s to arrive.

rescate.ayuda_viene: A support ship is coming: the trip back uses less oxygen.
rescate.encuentro: Itzel is exhausted and has very little air left.
rescate.itzel_dice: Itzel: Thanks for coming! On the Space Station, astronauts lose bone and muscle if they don't exercise. On the Moon, it's still being studied.
rescate.aire_pregunta: Itzel has almost no air. What do we do?

reserva.cuesta: − She waits alone while you go get another one.

rescate.regreso_pregunta: How do we get back to the base?
rescate.sin_rover: There's no rover: you left it at the rocks. You can only walk.
rescate.tormenta_sigue: The storm is still going: there's more radiation outside.

nota_aire.manguera: You shared your tank with Itzel ({o2} O2).
nota_aire.reserva: You left Itzel your reserve and went for another one ({o2} O2, +{rad} radiation).

nota_regreso.rover: You returned in the rover ({o2} O2).
nota_regreso.caminar: You walked back at Itzel's pace ({o2} O2, +{rad} radiation).

rescate.pregunta: Do we fix the radio to warn Earth now, or leave right away?
rescate.herida_si: With the first-aid kit, Itzel gets her strength back and walks better.
rescate.herida_no: Without a first-aid kit, Itzel walks slower (-{costo} O2).
rescate.nota_reparar: You fixed the radio: the data reached Earth in time.
rescate.nota_salir: You left fast; the data will arrive when you get back.
rescate.nota_herida: Without a first-aid kit, Itzel walked slower because she was tired, and we used more oxygen.
rescate.planta_texto: Chispa took care of this little plant at the base. It's real: in 2021, scientists planted this same plant (Arabidopsis) in lunar soil brought back by the Apollo 11, 12, and 17 missions. All the seeds sprouted! But they grew slower and got stressed, because lunar soil is very tough for plants.
rescate.nota_planta: Chispa brought his plant: growing plants in lunar soil is possible, but hard (NASA OSDR).

completa.texto: Everyone is safe. Earth protected its satellites: instead of blackouts, there are auroras in the sky. And Itzel's ice is already in the news.

sin_aviso.texto: Everyone is safe, but the alert didn't arrive. Some satellites fail for a few hours.
sin_aviso.voz: Itzel: Sometimes you have to choose: you saved them or us.

hielo_secreto.texto: Everyone is safe and Earth protected its satellites. But Itzel's discovery didn't arrive.
hielo_secreto.voz: Itzel: I'll come back for my ice! Will you come with me next time?

evacuacion.texto: An automatic ship picked everyone up. Nobody was left behind.
evacuacion.voz: Chispa: What cost us the most {recurso} was «{decision}» ({valor}). Next time will go better!

final.resumen_fuentes: NASA science in this game: {reales} real facts and {ejemplo} examples (not verified yet).
final.fuentes_sub: Real things NASA discovered that we used in the mission.

fuentes_ideas.Solar storm (CME): Sometimes the Sun throws a giant cloud of particles into space.
fuentes_ideas.Landing zone: We landed next to Shackleton crater, at the Moon's south pole.
fuentes_ideas.Craters the Sun never reaches: Some craters are so deep that the Sun never gets in. And they hold ice!
fuentes_ideas.Rescue routes: NASA has maps of the Moon to plan where to go.
fuentes_ideas.Rover speed: A south pole rover moves slower than you walk.
fuentes_ideas.Storm radiation: Far from Earth, the suit and shield protect us from radiation.
fuentes_ideas.Chispa's plant: Some little plants grew in soil brought from the Moon. But it was hard for them!
fuentes_ideas.Light at the south pole: There the Sun stays right on the horizon and shadows are super long.
fuentes_ideas.Cold in the crater: In the dark craters it's colder than 200 degrees below zero.
fuentes_ideas.Lunar dust on Apollo: Moon dust is super fine and sticks to everything, even the suits!
fuentes_ideas.Bone and muscle on the Space Station: Without gravity, bones and muscles get weaker. That's why you have to exercise.
fuentes_ideas.Plants that grow in space: Some seeds sprouted on the Space Station, with no gravity!
fuentes_ideas.The Apollo footprints are still on the M: The Moon has no wind: the Apollo footprints are still there.
fuentes_ideas.Moon's gravity (1.62 m/s²): On the Moon everything weighs one sixth as much as on Earth.

final.leyenda_fuentes: ✓ Real data: measured by NASA, with its page.  ⚠ EXAMPLE DATA: a test number we haven't verified yet. «Not live»: NASA didn't answer and we used a saved record. Tap a row to open its source.

final.insignia_mision: Rescue at the Lunar South Pole
final.exito: You saved Itzel and Chispa. Earth's satellites are protected!
final.fallo: It wasn't enough this time. Real astronauts practice many times too.
final.causa_oxigeno: Chispa: We ran out of oxygen (it reached {oxigeno})! Air is used up with every hour of travel and every climb. Next time try a shorter route, a suit that uses less air, or bring the extra tank.
final.causa_radiacion: Chispa: The solar storm caught us and radiation reached {radiacion} (the limit is 100). Next time charge the shield, use a suit that protects more, or take shelter before the storm arrives.

info.esclusa: Base airlock: we close it so we don't lose air. The mission is outside.
info.paneles: Solar panels: at the south pole the Sun stays very low, so they stand almost upright.
info.ciencia: Science vehicle: today it's collecting soil samples. It's not for the rescue.
info.carga: Cargo robot: it carries boxes between modules. It's too slow for the mission.

exterior.pendiente: Slow down. The ground has a steep slope.
exterior.rocas: Obstacle detected. Find a safe space to pass.
exterior.traccion_aviso: The wheels are losing traction. Reduce power.
exterior.bateria: We're using too much power. Plan the rest of the trip.
exterior.ruta_recuperada: Excellent! We're back on the route to Chispa.
exterior.crater_peligro: Careful! I detect a steep slope. Slow down or find another route.

tutorial.stella: Welcome to the lunar rover! I'm STELLA, your co-pilot. Use the controls to drive and follow the navigation beacons. Watch out for craters!

em.traccion_stella: Attention, astronaut! The wheels are slipping on the lunar regolith. If we keep speeding up, we could get stuck.
em.traccion_exito: Excellent move! We got our traction back. Now look for a safer route.
em.traccion_consejo: Tip: on loose regolith, go slowly. Speeding up hard only spins the wheels.
em.atasco_stella: Our vehicle is stuck. We can try to free the wheels with a special maneuver.
em.motores: Motors stopped. This way the wheels stop sinking.
em.modo_rec: Recovery mode on: now each wheel can move on its own.
em.maniobra_pregunta: Which traction maneuver do we use?
maniobras: Good! In wheel walking, some wheels move forward while the others hold the rover, like a little inchworm.
Speeding up hard only spins the wheels and sinks them deeper into the regolith.
Spinning out of control digs up the ground under the wheels. We need a coordinated move.
em.impulsos: Press SPACE or PUSH when the yellow mark passes over the ▼ zone. Pushes: {n}/3
em.impulso_mal: Almost. Wait until the mark is over the ▼ zone and try again.
em.impulsos_ok: The wheels moved together! Now let's back up to firm ground.
em.atasco_exito: We did it! You used a recovery maneuver inspired by space robotics.
em.atasco_consejo: These maneuvers help, but they don't work on every terrain. The safest thing is to go around very soft ground or drive in slowly.
em.dato_viper: The VIPER rover was designed with wheels that can turn and adjust their position independently to move better on difficult terrain.
em.dato_sim: Educational simulation: our R-1 rover is made up and has its own limits. VIPER was designed for slopes of about 15°.
em.crater_stella: Our rover is stuck. First we must check its stability before trying to move it.
em.analisis: Slope of {g}° and stability of {e}%. Look at the options and choose the safest one.
em.noA: The slope is {g}°: above {lim}° it's not safe to back out.
em.noB: There isn't enough stability or power to use the mobility systems safely.
em.noC: Let's use the rover's systems first. Assistance is for when they aren't safe or they fail.
em.A_proceso: The slope lets us get out. Backing up very slowly...
em.B_proceso: I'm turning on wheel walking to climb the edge little by little...
em.B_falla: The maneuver wasn't enough: the wheels can't find grip. Now we can ask for robotic assistance.
em.crater_exito: Rover stabilized! We got off the crater edge safely.
em.crater_consejo: Watching the route and braking in time prevents most accidents. Go around craters on flat ground!
em.asist_stella: Recovery isn't safe. I'll request robotic assistance from the lunar station.
em.asist_enlace: Linking with the lunar station... (made-up CoderWolf technology, not NASA's)
em.asist_camino: The helper robot is on its way. You stay safe inside the rover.
em.robot_llego: The helper robot arrived. First let's analyze the rover's position.
em.asist_apoyo_p: Where does the robot anchor itself?
apoyos: A loose rock on the edge
A loose rock could move when pulled. Let's find something firmer.
Correct! Firm, flat ground gives the best support.
Inside the crater the slope is steeper: the robot could slip too.
em.asist_remolque_p: How do we start the tow?
remolques: A sudden pull could flip the rover. Better go slow.
Good thinking! A slow tow keeps the rover stable.
em.robot_exito: Rescue complete! The helper robot took us to firm ground and is going back to the station.
em.reinicio: ↺ Rescue: go back to the last beacon
em.reinicio_stella: A rescue team took us to the last safe beacon. Your progress is saved: let's keep going!

crater_helado._nota: Escena CraterHelado (Rol 5). El traje aísla: el frío afecta al rover, no al astronauta.
crater_helado.intro: STELLA: We're entering a crater the Sun never reaches. Hold → (or click) to move forward.
crater_helado.intro_linterna: STELLA: Your flashlight shines far. That way we'll see the rocks in time.
crater_helado.intro_sin_linterna: STELLA: We didn't bring a flashlight. We can only see a little and we go slower.
crater_helado.dice_calef_si: STELLA: Heater on. The rover runs well, but it uses power and that costs us oxygen.
crater_helado.dice_calef_no: STELLA: Heater off. We save oxygen, but the cold will slow the rover down.
crater_helado.aviso_frio: STELLA: The rover is getting cold and slower! Your suit protects you, but the wheels and battery feel the cold.
crater_helado.aviso_polvo: STELLA: Dust is covering the rover's headlights and camera. We see less and could crash.
crater_helado.polvo_apolo: STELLA: Lunar dust is sharp and sticks to everything. On the Apollo missions it scratched visors and damaged equipment.
crater_helado.choque: Rock! We didn't see it in time (−{o2} O2).
crater_helado.avanzar: Hold → or click to move forward
crater_helado.fin_titulo: We got out of the crater!
crater_helado.consejo_choques: Tip: with clean dust and good light, you see the rocks in time.
crater_helado.consejo_frio: Tip: with the heater off for a long time, the rover crawls and the trip takes longer.
crater_helado.consejo_bien: Great job! You balanced light, heat, and time.
crater_helado.bitacora: You crossed the frozen crater: you used {o2} oxygen, hit {choques} rocks, and cleaned the dust {limpiezas} times.

huellas.intro: Look: there are two sets of wheel tracks. One is from Itzel's rover. The other is from a base cargo rover.
huellas.ficha: Itzel's rover is light with thin wheels. The cargo rover is heavy with wide wheels. Move the magnifying glass over the ? circles (with the mouse, the arrows, or by dragging your finger).
huellas.decidir: Each new clue costs {n} oxygen. If you choose right, we keep going without spending more. If you're wrong, we lose oxygen going back.

pistas.ancho_itzel: This wheel is thin: it's 2 squares wide.
pistas.ancho_carga: This wheel is wide: it's 4 squares wide.
pistas.prof_itzel: The track is shallow. The vehicle is light.
pistas.prof_carga: The track is very deep. The vehicle is heavy and sinks in.
pistas.obj_itzel: A purple glove next to the track! It has a white I.
pistas.obj_carga: There's only dust and pebbles here.

ayuda: See the circles with ? Move the magnifying glass over one and wait a moment.
Remember: heavy things sink more. Which track is shallower?
Look closely near the {lado} track. Something is shining there!
huellas.error: It's the base cargo rover! Itzel isn't here. Going back costs us {o2} oxygen.
huellas.volver: We're back at the fork. Now let's follow the other track.
huellas.bien: This is Itzel's track! Good thinking. Let's follow it!
huellas.bitacora_bien: Tracks: you followed Itzel's track on the first try ({pistas} clues checked).
huellas.bitacora_mal: Tracks: you first followed the cargo rover's track and lost {o2} oxygen ({pistas} clues checked).

rocas.intro: Huge rocks block the way. The rover can't drive over them.

rodear.gana: You keep the rover: shelter and an easy trip back.
rodear.cuesta: The way is long: you use more oxygen.

pie.gana: Short: you use less if you carry little.
pie.cuesta: The rover stays here: no shelter in the storm.

rocas.toca: Tap an option to see how much oxygen it costs.
rocas.blindado: With the armored suit you use more.
rocas.carga: You carry {kg} kg. On the Moon everything weighs one sixth as much: it feels like {luna} kg.
rocas.soltar: Tap an object below to leave it.
rocas.resultado_rodear: You went around the rocks in the rover. You used {o2} oxygen.
rocas.resultado_pie: You crossed in little hops. You used {o2} oxygen. The rover stays here.
rocas.bitacora_rodear: Rocks: you went around in the rover ({o2} O2).
rocas.bitacora_pie: Rocks: you crossed on foot with {kg} kg ({o2} O2) and left the rover.

tormenta.info: Sun cloud from {fecha} at {vel} km/s. It lasts about {horas} h.
tormenta.toca: Tap an option to see how many particles it stops.

saliente.gana: Protects a lot, but not everything.
saliente.cuesta: You have to detour and wait.

seguir.cuesta: Only the suit and shield protect you.

tormenta.sin_rover: There's no rover: you left it at the rocks.
tormenta.sin_comida: Without food, waiting is more tiring ({o2} O2).
tormenta.personal: Your suit and shield stop {n} out of 10.
tormenta.stella: STELLA: The storm is here! These are very fast particles coming from the Sun.
tormenta.resultado: We got +{rad} radiation and used {o2} oxygen.
tormenta.resultado_seguir: We keep walking. We'll reach Itzel sooner, but the storm is still going.
tormenta.resultado_refugio: The worst of the storm has passed. Itzel waited {horas} h more.
tormenta.bitacora: Storm: {nombre}. We got +{rad} radiation and used {o2} oxygen.
tormenta.nota_simplificacion: Simplified: in reality the fastest particles can arrive before the cloud.

diario._nota: Diario de misión (escena Diario). Frases en primera persona, cortas, para 7 a 12 años.
diario.costo_nada: It didn't cost me any air.
diario.ysi_simulado: If I had chosen to {decision}, I would have ended with {o2} air and {rad} radiation.
diario.ysi_evacuacion: And they would have had to evacuate us!

mochila.texto: I filled my backpack with: {objetos}. It weighed {kg} kg.
mochila.linterna_si: I took the flashlight to see in the dark.
mochila.linterna_no: I didn't take a flashlight. The dark was going to be hard.
mochila.ysi_linterna: With the flashlight, the dark path would have been easier.
mochila.ysi_escudo: With the shield, the storm would have hurt me less.

equipo.texto: I wore the {traje} and flew in the {nave}.
equipo.efecto: My gear protected me from radiation: {n} out of 10 parts.

ysi.blindado: With the light suit I would have used less air, but I'd be less protected.
ysi.ligero: With the armored suit I'd be more protected, but I'd use more air.

ruta.crater: I went through the crater. It was short, but dark and steep.
ruta.cresta: I went along the ridge. It was long, but flat and sunlit.

ysi.crater: Along the ridge I would have had light, but been slower and gotten more radiation.
ysi.cresta: Through the crater I would have arrived sooner, but in the dark and cold.

crater.texto: I crossed the frozen crater in the rover.
crater.ysi: If I had gone slower, I would have crashed less and used less air.

huellas.bien: I found Itzel's tracks on the first try.
huellas.mal: First I followed the cargo rover's tracks. I was wrong and lost air.
huellas.ysi_mal: If I had checked more clues before choosing, I would have saved air.

rocas.pie: I left the rover and crossed the rocks on foot.
rocas.rodear: I went around the rocks in the rover.

ysi.pie: With the rover I'd have had a shelter, but the way was long.
ysi.rodear: On foot I would have arrived sooner, but with no shelter.

tormenta.saliente: I hid under a rock overhang. It protected a lot, but I had to detour.
tormenta.rover: I took shelter under the rover. It protected me a little.
tormenta.seguir: I kept going to Itzel in the middle of the storm.

ysi.saliente: If I had kept going, I'd have arrived sooner, but with much more radiation.
ysi.rover: Under the rock overhang I would have been better protected.
ysi.seguir: Under the rock overhang I would have been much better protected.

aire.manguera: I shared my tank with Itzel. We stayed together.
aire.reserva: I left Itzel my reserve and went for another one.

ysi.manguera: With the reserve I would have used less air, but Itzel would have waited alone.
ysi.reserva: Sharing the tank, we'd stay together, but I'd use more air.

mensajes.texto: I sent these messages to Earth: {lista}.

regreso.rover: We came back in the rover. It was fast.
regreso.caminar: We walked back at Itzel's pace.
regreso.sin_rover: Without the rover, walking was the only way back.

planta.texto: Chispa gave me a little leaf from his plant. I stuck it here.
planta.curiosidad: In 2015 some tiny seeds traveled to the Space Station. Up there they sprouted without gravity!
